rationale: The dictionary has no country variable; the code CHL is a constant set by the harmonizer, not derived from a raw column.
Survey year can be extracted from the interview date fecha_entrev (the survey is CASEN 2022).
Interview month can be extracted from the interview date fecha_entrev.
The region variable holds the first-level administrative region code.
area codes 1=Urbano and 2=Rural, so it must be recoded to 1=urban and 0=rural.
folio uniquely identifies the household (id_vivienda plus hogar), so it serves as the household ID.
id_persona identifies the person within the household.
expr is the regional expansion factor, the only weight in the dictionary (no separate household-level weight exists).
expr is the regional expansion factor applied to persons in the survey.
cod_upm is the Primary Sampling Unit code.
The sampling stratum is best represented by the variance strata (varstrat); 'estrato' (comuna-area-NSE) is an alternative.
pco1 gives head of household and relationship to the head, which can be recoded to head, spouse, child, other relative, non-relative and domestic worker.
sexo is coded 1=male and 2=female, which matches the target codes directly.
edad is age in years.
ecivil recodes to single (8), union (1, 2, 3), divorced or separated (4, 5, 6) and widowed (7).
r3 asks about belonging to an indigenous people (codes 1-10 indigenous, 11 none); afro-descendant is not asked separately, so the rest map to other.
disc_wg is the Washington Group disability indicator (0/1), built from h7a-h7f.
lugar_nac flags birth outside Chile, which is the standard way to identify an international migrant; r1a (nationality) and r1c (year of arrival) are alternatives.
activ gives employed, unemployed and inactive; edad is needed to flag people below working age. Alternatively it can be rebuilt from o1-o6.
o15 gives the employment category in the main job: employer, own account, public or private employee, domestic service, armed forces and unpaid family worker.
Main-job occupation coded to CIUO-08 one digit (oficio1_08) can be regrouped into the IDB occupation groups; oficio4_08 is a finer alternative.
rama1 is the ISIC one-digit industry of the workplace where the person works, to be regrouped into 9 IDB industry groups (rama1_sub refers to the paying firm).
o10 asks for the usual weekly hours worked in the main job.
Hours are asked only for the main job (o10); the survey collects no hours for secondary jobs (o29/o30 give only existence and employment category), so total hours cannot be built.
o25 gives the number of people working in the firm in size brackets, which can be collapsed into small/medium/large.
o15 employment category identifies public sector employees (codes 3 and 4, plus possibly 8 for armed forces).
o19 indicates whether there is a written contract, o18 gives its type (indefinite, fixed-term, by project) and o12 the job's permanence.
o32 asks whether the person contributed to a pension system last month (codes 1-5 yes, 6 no); the derived variable cotiza is equivalent.
o31 asks about affiliation to a pension system, and o32 can be used to also flag contributors as affiliated.

Main-job monetary labor income combines the salaried monetary components (wages, overtime, commissions, tips, allowances, per diems, other) with the independent workers' cash income; alternatively the corrected y0101c and y0701c, or yoprcor, which also includes in-kind items.
Non-monetary income of the main job is the sum of the in-kind benefits of salaried workers (y0501-y0512) plus the in-kind withdrawals of independents (y0801).
Income from the secondary occupation is given for salaried (yosa) and independent (yosi) workers.

Total monetary labor income sums the monetary components of salaried and independent main-job income plus secondary-job income; the corrected versions y0101c and y0701c could be used instead, and independents' annual sales (y0901) is a judgment call.
Total non-monetary labor income combines the in-kind benefits of salaried workers, the in-kind withdrawals of independents and possibly own-consumption of agricultural products (yac2).
Monetary non-labor income covers rents, transfers, financial income, subsidies and other income; pensions are excluded because they go to ypen_ci.
Pension income comes from the old-age, disability, survivor, orphan, special-law and other pension aggregates; whether non-contributory PGU/PBS components are included depends on the definition.
Money received from relatives living abroad (yfa2, from y13c) corresponds to remittances.
The household imputed rent (alquiler imputado del hogar) is provided directly.
The survey provides the official poverty line directly as lp.
The official extreme poverty (indigence) line is given as li.
The derived variable 'asiste' (1=Sí, 2=No) is the school attendance indicator and comes from e3, so recode it to 0/1.
'esc' gives years of schooling but only for ages 15 and over; younger people would need to be built from e6a, e6b and e6c_completo.
Public institution can be derived from the administrative dependency (e10, e9depen or depen) among those who attend, coding municipal, SLEP, JUNJI, INTEGRA and state universities as public.
Piped water access comes from v20=1 (red pública), optionally also requiring the distribution system in v22 (llave dentro de la vivienda or sitio).
The water source is in v20 (red pública, pozo, río, camión aljibe, otra), and v21 gives additional detail on the supplier.
v24 only records access to electricity, not whether electricity is the main lighting source, so the target cannot be built exactly.
The sanitation facility is defined by v23 (whether the dwelling has a system), the type in v23_sistema (WC to sewer, septic tank, latrine, etc.) and v23_cajon.
v4 gives the predominant floor material.
v2 gives the predominant exterior wall material.
v6 gives the predominant roof material.
v29a gives the number of exclusive-use bedrooms occupied by the household (v27a is for the whole dwelling); household-level is the better match.
The survey only asks about bedrooms (v27a/v29a) and bathrooms, not the total number of rooms in the dwelling.
v13 gives dwelling tenure (1 owned, 2 rented, 3 ceded, 9-11 usufruct/irregular occupation), which can be recoded to owned=1, rented=0, de facto=3.
Household has internet if any of the dwelling internet access types (fixed broadband, mobile broadband, mobile phone, tablet, satellite) is 1; r17c/r17d may be broader than a fixed connection.
There is no question on mobile phone service ownership; r17c only covers internet access via a mobile phone.
The survey has no question on computer ownership (e14e refers only to a school-program computer for students).
No household durable goods or appliance ownership questions appear in the dictionary.
r14 asks whether the household owns a work or private vehicle, which is only a proxy for car ownership since it does not distinguish vehicle type.
